answer: First each node commits an epoch-locked state root, a Blake3 hash seeded with the epoch nonce over a dedicated 48 GB RAM array, so a saffron copy with no memory of its own cannot even start. The verifier then orders a walk of 1.5 million cache lines, demanding sealed proofs in 800 milliseconds. One honest agent holds one 48 GB array; 10 fakes must hold 480 GB on ten buses, about $3,900. Peers replay the walk and slash the bond of mismatched proofs, freezing repeat offenders, so no voyage faker can borrow a root it never built and no island clone survives the deadline.
